result:
**Decision: CONTINUE.** The next task is round 290, the scheduled RETRO covering rounds 275–289. It changes no app code: A implements nothing, and C checks that every number and claim in the retro traces to a file. The advisor was available; I consulted it before starting and again at the end, and applied its three fixes.

**Round 289 (FIX-PD-1b) is done.** C passed all 13 rows at both viewports with `browserVerified` and `realVerified` both true and 0 bugs, and gate 289 published `5a911ff`. That commit is the round-290 baseline. F7 and SR-230-6 are closed. Four older findings (C-R282-01/02/03 and A-R282-REVIEW-DW11) were fixed and published in round 283 but still read "fix dispatched", so I closed them in the backlog.

**Gate 289 raised two Mediums**, so round 291 is a fix-up (FIX-PD-1b2), all in `ArrangementLibrary.tsx` plus a doc and test names:
- GATE289-S1: screen readers may read the new group heading twice; the fix is `aria-hidden`.
- GATE289-S2: doc 216 says the collection name "always shows", which is false for single-collection results.
- Two cheap Lows ride along: the group keys (GATE289-S3) and stale test names (A-R289-REVIEW-L2).
- The product half of S2 (should a single collection still get a heading?) goes to Saba as SABA-Q-LIB-SINGLE-RUN.

**What RETRO 290 found** (window 275–289, $358.81):
- **C PASS 12, FAIL 3, plus one gate failure** (round 276). All four came from B (me), not A: a missed item in the last retro, a sweep that skipped test files, a pre-check that didn't run the specified test rows, and two clauses in one task that contradicted each other.
- **B accounts for 51% of the cost.**
- **Last retro's SWEEP experiment is refuted:** GATE276-T1 was a Medium in a task that had the sweep.
- **The row-severity idea is rejected on its own adoption rule:** round 287 failed on a Low that still needed fix-up round 288. `tech-lead` wanted to keep testing it; that disagreement is recorded in the retro.
- **New experiment:** every artifact a task cites must exist and be checked with `test -f`. It was proposed by `consequence-tester`, and C records new fields for it from round 290.
- **`lessons.md` is now 59 lines:** L27 merged into L52, L17 folded into L2, a new L56 (cited artifacts must exist), and a ruling-line clause in L4.
- **New systemic task SYS-VACUOUS-ROWS** closes four deferred Lows that share one cause: test rows no mutant can turn red.
- **Manual check moved:** TLM-R274's deadline passed without an answer, so it is now on Saba's final manual-check list. It does not block rounds.

**Screen and journey review:** I captured product page → Studio → export on the mock backend at both viewports and stopped the mock afterwards. Ten candidates (SR-290-1…10) are in `user-review/screen-review-290.md` for Saba; none will be built without his answer.
- My capture script's lane click hit the pan slider, so the journey screenshots show the stems on the wrong lane. A separate probe confirmed the real behaviour behind SR-290-3: Music is active by default, so a first-visit Add puts a stem on Music. The review states this openly.
- The toolbar wrapping to two rows at 1280 is not new; it is already Saba's open question SABA-Q-9-TRANSPORT.

The store tree is unchanged (`sha256sum -c` rc 0, clean status).

**Next after round 291:** REGRESSION (due on or after 2026-11-02, after the Medium fix), FIX-PD-1c, SYS-VACUOUS-ROWS, STUDIO-LINK, NAME-AND-HINT, then STUDIO-PERFORMANCE. No frontend-architect checkpoint is needed now.
